newsitem.title: USA: American Airline pilots board may vote mid afternoon.
newsitem.headline: American Airline pilots board may vote mid afternoon.

text.p: The board of American Airlines pilots union said on Thursday it might vote this afternoon on a labor contract proposed by the carrier.

"After the working the lunch, the board will begin its debate and they could vote mid afternoon," said Wally Pitts, a spokesman for the Allied Pilots Association, which represents 9,300 American Airlines pilots.

Pitts said he is "unaware of any other items on the agenda," and added, "it is most likely the meeting scheduled for Friday would be cancelled if the contract proposal is approved." The board had scheduled meetings Thursday and Friday.
The 18-member board of the APA is meeting in suburban Chicago to vote on American Airlines' contract proposal.
American Airlines is a subsidiary of AMR Corp.
